quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue was $168.8 million, up 23% from $137.2 million in the previous quarter and up 55% from $108.8 million a year ago; infrastructure (approximately $85 million) is now the largest revenue category and grew 145% year-over-year on production ramps of optical data-center platforms; non-GAAP gross margin 59.5% and GAAP EPS $0.02, a return to GAAP profitability.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $168.8 million, +55% YoY, +23% QoQ; infrastructure ~$85 million, +145% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 optical data center revenue expectation raised again to $210 million-$230 million (an increase of more than $50 million, all driven by the Keystone product family, none from Washington or Annapurna) based on robust customer orders and rising visibility of program ramps, with continued growth as run rates expand into 2027; order visibility is about six months given tight supply and increasing demand.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 optical data center revenue $210 million-$230 million

quarterly_data.signal: Keystone, the 100 Gb per lane 5 nm CMOS PAM4 DSP and SerDes, continues to ramp into high-volume production at major hyperscale customers across U.S. and Asia for 400 Gb and 800 Gb deployments, delivering almost 40% lower power consumption than competition; all the revenue growth now is driven by 800 Gb, which becomes substantially the bigger portion of run-rate revenue into 2027; MaxLinear says it is now designing across the board of all optical module players on 800 Gb and is one of only three PAM4 DSP players with a track record of millions of units shipped.
quarterly_data.figure: almost 40% lower power than competition; growth now 800 Gb-driven

quarterly_data.signal: Rushmore, the 1.6 Tb optical PAM4 DSP at 200 Gb per lane, is sampling with substantial performance and power advantages and a unique supply-chain diversification versus competition; it is expected to become an important optical connectivity growth driver beginning in 2027 — initial ramps at one or two opportunities in the second half of 2027, layering through 2028 and 2029 — with ASP upside at the higher speed, while the same Keystone customers are working toward deploying 1.6 Tb and 800 Gb keeps growing alongside.

Portfolio expanded beyond PAM4 DSPs to TIAs, drivers and onboard retimers covering pluggable, LRO, LPO, NPO and NCPO architectures: Washington (200 Gb per lane TIA, standalone for LPO/NPO or paired with Rushmore) and Annapurna (200 Gb per lane Ethernet retimer for 1.6 Tb active electrical cables and onboard retimers in scale-up racks/switches) expect initial revenue in 2027 and a more meaningful volume ramp in 2028; also a first XGS-PON hyperscaler design win for data center control plane (qualified for a 2027 ramp), USB bridge controller wins at two major hyperscalers for AI rack management, and Panther storage accelerators expected to roughly double in 2026 and nearly double again in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Washington/Annapurna initial revenue 2027, ramp 2028; Panther ~2x in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Cash of approximately $93.7 million reflects a substantial wafer prepayment supporting rising data-center demand, for which order backlog is increasing in the second half and into 2027 (backlog out a couple of quarters, orders now being placed for Q1); supply is tight and wafer, packaging and test costs are rising (purchase obligations up about $40 million), with foundry and OSAT partners described as incredibly supportive; Keystone is called the only 5 nm SoC shipping in volume at 100 Gb per lane.
quarterly_data.figure: cash ~$93.7 million after wafer prepayment; purchase obligations up ~$40 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $210 million-$220 million with growth from all four segments and particular strength in infrastructure driven by data center optical interconnects; non-GAAP gross margin guided to 58.5%-61.5% (60% at the midpoint, ahead of schedule) on the mix shift to infrastructure; long-term targets remain 65% gross margin and 30%-35% operating margin.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $210 million-$220 million; non-GAAP gross margin 60% midpoint

quarterly_data.signal: No 10% customer; optical customers span U.S. and Asia hyperscalers, Tier 1 data center customers, OEMs and a number of optical module makers (names not disclosed); management expects more concentration as a handful of customers drive most volume over the next six quarters, and attributes the raised outlook to market share gains on top of TAM growth.
